description: Ask-path eval (WS-03, WS-10, EXE-01, AGT-01, G-10, AGT-06, tier real_agent): the object workspace's Ask through its one path (operator_ui.object_workspace.ObjectWorkspace.ask_run, the path the console's ask shows: its 1000-character question limit, the plx.object root check, operating.agent_loop.run unchanged over the reader's HostAccess.agent_server with read-only ontology tools, its bounds, the evidence rule and the claim gate (operating.answer_gate: each structured claim checked by reference against the cell it cites in a record the session returned, a value resting only on lead-tier links passing only marked a lead; the answer text rendered by code from the claims shown, never the planner's prose as written), the filter of claims citing a record the workspace withholds and the no_cited_claims downgrade) with a headless Claude Code planner (operating.agent_loop.ClaudeCodePlanner, as operator_ui.case_console --ask wires it; the operator's Claude Code login, no paid API), rooted at each item's root as the workspace roots it. Items: live_bc, the same admitted items as eval.real_agent (at least 20 Business-Central-rooted oracle items whose root the named reader in PLX_EVAL_READER resolves through the persistent host, each session the console's workspace for that reader over the case runtime and verified reader of the host's own MCP start-up in process (a fresh single-use agent ticket signed with PLX_WORKBENCH_SESSION_SECRET); without the identity the part reads as the declared eval principal (operating.eval_principal, examples/eval_principal.json: staff:operations and staff:sales, no marking, no action path), labelled reader eval_principal in the result; the A6 permission proof (denied_leaks) is never made by it and still requires PLX_EVAL_READER), then the pinned 10-item FIXTURE_SAMPLE of evals/dev on the fixture world. Per item the reader's plx.find picks the root; a root it does not name, or the workspace's root check does not show, is withheld and gets no session slot (blocked, roots_withheld). Only the claims the workspace shows are scored: the answer (shown claims' value claims, '<gap state>: <subject>' unknowns) is scored by evals/score.py on the harness's re-reads as the reader, the same scorer and read-gap rule as eval.real_agent. Each session record carries the effective agent definition's stamp (_meta plx/agent: id, version, digest from operating/agent_definitions.json) and its stop (outcome, reason, class). Reports per part correct / wrong / blocked / justified abstention with coverage beside accuracy, confident_unsupported (stated answers the claim gate refused), and ask: stop classes, the distinct agent stamps, withheld roots, failed sessions, withheld claims (kept, not shown, never scored), unsupported claims and context reuse (verified/reviewed link and identity tiers and review decisions the session's tool results carried), with eval.tiers keeping access / capture / projection / deterministic / agent apart. Counts, rates and enums only; transcripts stay in {tmp}.
notes: live-unverified until a passing live-check result; no Ask answer from a model is recorded until this check runs. Keyless tests drive it with a scripted planner (tests/test_eval_real_agent.py: on every fixture-sample item the eval and the console's own workspace for the reader give the same outcome and shown claims, a kept claim citing a record the workspace withholds is not scored and is counted; a session whose start-up is refused, that raises, whose planner fails after a usable reply or whose workspace fails to close (its session host closed all the same) is blocked with its code while the run goes on, and a withheld root uses no session slot; a live host's projection store that is missing, projected from another mirror generation or unverifiable blocks the live part once at start-up (ask_needs_a_projection_store, ontology_store_refused), before any source read or session; through the ask command on the fixture world a correct answer scores correct, a value the claim gate refuses is unsupported (confident_unsupported, scored an unjustified abstention), an escalation is scored with its stop class, a root the reader cannot see gets no session; on a persistent host's own state the Ask session is the host's MCP server for the named reader in process, its ticket never left in the environment). requires_env_any CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / PLX_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN only (without both the check is skipped); the reader identity, session secret, host state and BC/Graph names are optional_env: until the operator names a real employee reader the live part reads as the eval principal (labelled, never the A6 permission proof), with the fixture sample recorded beside it. No binary, or sessions that all fail without an answer (a planner that cannot start), is blocked (host_misconfiguration). The fixture sample's projection is recorded at the fixture world's now (2099), so its sessions read it at that now, as the deterministic baseline beside it does; live sessions read at the real now. Budget: at most 34 sessions (24 live, 10 fixture; k=1), each at most 8 planner turns of at most 120 s inside 300 s (later turns escalate session_time_exhausted), all started inside 4700 s, after the reader check (60 s), the oracle's live reads (900 s), the root probe (300 s) and the deterministic path (600 s): 6560 s plus at most one 300 s session overrun, 140 s under the 7000 s check timeout (eval.real_agent has its own 7000 s). A session the budget refuses is blocked and the run incomplete (exit 3); exit 3 also when fewer than 8 runs were scored, the live oracle sampled fewer than 20 items, or read-gap runs exceed 10% of every run or of any one part's runs (eval.fail_reasons blocked_tripwire, the dev baseline's rule; each part reports blocked_share and blocked_tripwire; a read gap is our capture tier's, so it stays red); fewer than 20 roots the reader resolves is blocked (roots_unresolved), never a pass. Context reuse (AGT-01) is measured, never asserted: eval.live_bc.ask.context_reuse counts the verified and reviewed tiers and review decisions the session's tool results carried. Daily at most: it spends the operator's Claude Code plan. The Claude Code login is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or its alias PLX_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (requires_env_any; operating.agent_environment gives the agent session the alias's value as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN when the canonical name is absent or empty, for an environment whose Claude Code session hides its own token from tool subprocesses). B1: the check passes only when eval.total meets accuracy >= 0.8, coverage >= 0.8 and confident_unsupported_rate <= 0.02. A blocked part (a refused host config or reader, a Portal outage) does not excuse the parts that ran: expect_blocked holds eval.total, the parts that ran, to the same bar, so a blocked run whose fixture parts miss it fails. Only a run no agent session answered (agent_unmeasured binary_not_found or every_session_failed, blocked_when) is blocked whole.
